topStories.headline: Manny Yekutiel Quits District 8 Race After New Assault Claims — His Mission Café at the Center of the Story
topStories.dek: The owner of Valencia Street's Manny's dropped out of the supervisor race Thursday after two more men accused him of sexual assault, triggering a cascade of endorsement withdrawals including Mayor Lurie's.
topStories.body:
Manny Yekutiel, the owner of the Mission District café and event space Manny's on Valencia Street and the frontrunner in the race for District 8 supervisor, ended his campaign on Thursday, October 1, hours after the San Francisco Standard published new sexual assault allegations against him. Mayor Daniel Lurie and six city supervisors rescinded their endorsements within hours; labor unions and advocacy groups including GrowSF followed.

Yekutiel had previously denied an earlier allegation made in June by political organizer Brad Chapin. Lurie had given him the benefit of the doubt after Yekutiel denied the claim directly to him. Thursday's report described two men — Ryan Clark and his partner — who told the Standard that Yekutiel had groped them at a Pride party in 2023, allegations that closely matched Chapin's account. The cascade of withdrawals made his continued candidacy untenable, and Yekutiel suspended his campaign by Thursday afternoon.

Despite dropping out, Yekutiel's name will remain on the November ballot; the deadline to withdraw passed in June. The San Francisco Democratic Party, which had already mailed endorsement materials supporting him, called a special meeting for October 11 to reconsider its position. Gary McCoy, a former aide to Rep. Nancy Pelosi, is now considered the presumed frontrunner in District 8, which covers the Castro and Noe Valley. McCoy has formed an alliance with rival Darshini Patel; both, along with Michael Nguyen, had publicly called for Yekutiel to step aside.

For the Mission neighborhood, the episode has a particular local dimension. Manny's on Valencia Street has been a prominent gathering place for political figures and neighbors, and Yekutiel co-founded the Civic Joy Fund, which helps support the Valencia Live! street party series. The program's final night of the 2026 season is scheduled for October 8.

topStories.headline: Mission Residents Confront SFPD Captain Over Open Drug Use, Officers Who Drive Past Without Acting
topStories.dek: At the Mission Station's monthly community meeting, Captain Sean Perdomo heard an earful about open drug use on neighborhood side streets and promised more foot patrols — while being candid about what the law allows officers to do.
topStories.body:
For nearly an hour at SFPD Mission Station's most recent monthly community meeting, Captain Sean Perdomo took questions from several dozen residents, merchants, and repeat attendees who said conditions on several neighborhood blocks have not improved despite ongoing complaints. The session, reported by Mission Local, centered on familiar concerns: open drug use at all hours on stretches of Albion, San Carlos, and Woodward streets; dirty sidewalks; and officers who residents said appeared to drive past violations without stepping out of their vehicles.

Perdomo acknowledged he had personally observed the same scenes over the past several months and said he would direct officers to patrol those blocks more regularly. But he was direct about the limits of what police can do: officers must personally witness a violation and have sufficient evidence before they can cite or arrest anyone, and cannot act on what they did not see. When residents said that officers seemed only to move people along, Perdomo said the expectation is that officers act on observed violations — and 'not just shoo them away' — while acknowledging officers are constrained by law.

One resident raised concern that some of the people visibly using drugs in the area appeared to be quite young. Perdomo said he did not yet know what was driving the trend but committed to increased patrols. The meeting captured a persistent tension in the Mission: as Perdomo noted, the district spans a wide economic spectrum — residents hold sharply different views on how public drug use should be addressed, and enforcement tools are narrower than many community members expect.

SFPD Mission Station holds community meetings on the last Tuesday of each month at various locations. The next scheduled date has not yet been posted on the department's website.

topStories.headline: Open Studios Weekend Puts Mission and Bernal Heights Artists in the Spotlight Saturday and Sunday
topStories.dek: ArtSpan's 52nd annual SF Open Studios focuses on the Mission, Bernal Heights, Castro, and Glen Park this weekend, with studios, art complexes, and historic spaces open free to the public.
topStories.body:
ArtSpan's 52nd San Francisco Open Studios program turns its attention to its District 2 — the Mission, Bernal Heights, Castro, Glen Park, and Noe Valley — this Saturday and Sunday, October 3 and 4, with participating artists' studios open from 11 a.m. to 5 p.m. The event is free to the public and is the nation's longest-running open studio program of its kind.

Project Artaud, the Mission arts complex at 450 Florida Street that has housed artists in a converted 1924 factory since 1971, is opening its entire block both days for studio tours, workshops, performances, and art sales. The complex is one of San Francisco's leading artist communities, housing four performance spaces and more than ten creative nonprofits. A short distance away, 1890 Bryant Street Studios — three floors of studios in a historic building — is also open Friday through Sunday under the theme 'Art Made Here,' with seasoned artists and emerging makers showing work that has been exhibited internationally alongside newer voices.

Addresses of participating studios across the Mission and Bernal Heights area are listed in the ArtSpan printed guide, available at local art institutions, and on the ArtSpan website at artspan.org. The Open Studios season continues through October 25, with each remaining weekend focused on different parts of the city; this weekend is the only one centered on these neighborhoods.

events.title: ArtSpan Open Studios — Mission, Bernal Heights & Castro District
events.location: Studios across Mission, Bernal Heights, Castro, Glen Park, and Noe Valley
events.description: District 2 of ArtSpan's 52nd annual SF Open Studios is free and self-guided; pick up a printed map at local art venues or visit artspan.org. Project Artaud (450 Florida St.) opens its full complex both days for tours, workshops, and art sales.

events.title: MAPP: Mission Arts Performance Project — October Crawl
events.location: Multiple venues near 24th Street, Mission District
events.description: The free bimonthly art, poetry, and concert crawl through the Mission features live music, storytelling, theater, and dance at venues around 24th Street. No tickets needed; find the schedule at the Mission Arts Performance Project's social media pages.

events.title: Valencia Live! — Final Night Market of 2026
events.location: Valencia Street between 18th and 21st Streets, Mission District
events.description: The free, all-ages monthly street party closes out its 2026 season with live music curated by Carnaval SF, salsa lessons with Grace Towers and Sara Fe, a Lotería Zone hosted by Mission Lotería, outdoor dining, and pop-up vendors; Valencia Street is car-free for the evening.

events.title: Litquake Literary Festival — Mission District Events
events.location: Multiple Mission District venues including 826 Valencia, Make-Out Room, The Chapel, Writers Grotto
events.description: The 27th Litquake festival runs citywide October 8–24 and culminates in the free Lit Crawl — billed as the world's largest literary pub crawl — on Saturday, October 24, 5–9 p.m., spreading across bars, galleries, and bookstores on and around Valencia Street.

events.title: Closing Weeks: Andy Vogt and Amy Trachtenberg at 500 Capp Street
events.time: Noon–5:00 PM (Fridays & Saturdays); guided tours Saturdays at 4:00 PM ($20)
events.location: 500 Capp Street (David Ireland House), Mission District
events.description: Final weeks to see dual exhibitions — Andy Vogt's 'The Ringing in My Eyes' and Amy Trachtenberg's 'Abstract Objects of Devotion' — installed inside the late conceptual artist David Ireland's historic Mission District home. Self-guided tours are free on Fridays and Saturdays.

events.title: In Their Name: Día de los Muertos 2026 — SOMArts Opening
events.location: SOMArts Cultural Center, 934 Brannan Street (near Mission District)
events.description: SOMArts opens its annual Día de los Muertos exhibition October 24; co-curator Rio Yañez, a Mission District native and son of the late artist René Yañez who co-founded the tradition, described this year's theme as a response to current events through honoring the dead.

events.title: 45th Annual Día de los Muertos Procession in the Mission
events.location: Starting at 22nd and Bryant Streets, Mission District
events.description: El Colectivo del Rescate Cultural leads the community procession from 22nd and Bryant south to 24th Street, west to Mission Street, and back — with Aztec dancers, musicians, and hundreds of participants honoring deceased loved ones. Free and open to all.

moreNews.headline: Deadline Tuesday: Affordable Housing Applications at 3300 Mission Street Close October 6
moreNews.body: The Bernal Heights Neighborhood Center is reminding residents that applications for affordable units at 3300 Mission Street — a 100-percent affordable housing development — close on Tuesday, October 6, 2026. The application and further details are available at bhnc.org.
